adjudicated.jp: 扉を開くのに、少しだけためらいがあった。
adjudicated.en: On going to open the door there was just a bit of hesitation.
comments: These need to all fit CCB0005 as well. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The slight hesitation before opening the door is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 今さらどの面さげて、と思いもする。
adjudicated.en: And I also thought, how could one do this after all that?
adjudicated.assessment: The hesitation about acting after everything that has happened remains, but どの面さげて specifically asks how he can show his face now. 'How could one do this' removes the first-person shame and replaces the face-to-face social idiom with a generic action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Part of me wondered how I could show my face there now, after everything.'

adjudicated.jp: が、人間は気分の生き物で、今朝はそんな気分だったから。
adjudicated.en: Yet humans are animals of mood, and this morning that was the mood.
adjudicated.assessment: The explanation that people are creatures of mood and that he happened to feel that way this morning is preserved despite literal phrasing.

adjudicated.jp: 自分への説明はそれで充分だ。
adjudicated.en: For myself, that is explanation enough.
comments: And rationalization. Notice that right now Misato should be REALLY pissed at Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: That rationale being sufficient as an explanation to himself is conveyed directly.

adjudicated.jp: けど先輩は、どう思うだろう。
adjudicated.en: But what will Senpai even think?
adjudicated.assessment: His wondering what the senior will think is preserved; 'even' adds conversational emphasis.

adjudicated.jp: 少し気になってしまった。
adjudicated.en: That was a little bit worrying.
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes him finding himself a little concerned or unable not to wonder. 'That was worrying' externalizes the concern as a property of the situation and loses the involuntary nuance of しまった.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I couldn't help wondering a little.'

adjudicated.jp: ノブをひねって、鉄扉を押し出す。
adjudicated.en: Turning the handle, I push out the iron door.
adjudicated.assessment: Turning the knob and pushing open the metal door are both preserved; 'push out' is unidiomatic but recoverable.

adjudicated.jp: 風が吹いた。
adjudicated.en: The wind blew,
comments: "Wind" is also "pretension/deception". In my first altogether-too-adapted version, I experimented with using "bluff", which the wind doesn't do but sorta-sounds like it should, but decided against it in revisions. It's completely impossible to notice unless considering the meta-implications of the rooftop being the place closest to Heaven but the hokora, and metaphorically, the place where interpersonal communication takes place - the wind is part of the disturbance, the lies, the communicative difficulties, the language barries, and all that that the exposure to the elements (sun as well) and the Penelopean (sysyphean?) effort of the building of the antenna.
Plus all the meta stuff about Misato. In short, it would go in the explanation anyway. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The wind blowing is preserved as the opening fragment of the following sentence.

adjudicated.jp: ちょうど踏み出た瞬間に。
adjudicated.en: on the exact instant I stepped outside.
comments: The implication is that the wind started when he was there. Hallucination in part, in part hints at the above interpretation(s). Which may just be hallucinated because his hallucinations still betray a truer reality. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The timing—just as he stepped outside—is preserved, though 'on the exact instant' is stiff.

adjudicated.jp: だが不思議と、晴れ晴れとした気分にさせてくれた。
adjudicated.en: But, inexplicably, that made me feel all bright and cheerful.
adjudicated.assessment: The inexplicable sense of brightness and relief produced by the moment is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 目線の先、広々とした給水塔が階段とは別にあって、その土台を共有して、大きなアンテナが立っていた。
adjudicated.en: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.
comments: This line is odd. The water tower described as "spacious" seems just not appropriate. I'm sort of forcing this reading, because it does sound like it's being described as separate from the staircase, which contradicts the BG of the outside of the school: the water tower is clearly on top of the staircase.

And the antenna is clearly on a different level from the staircase, so how it can share foundation I simply don't know. Plus there's those three steps before the antenna, so, dunno. Anyway, there are Two Towers in this place close to God and the outside world: it's a Tolkien reference. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source places the water tower apart from the stairwell and says the antenna shares the tower's foundation. The English instead places the water tower 'on the staircase' and makes the antenna stand apart from the tower, reversing the spatial relations in the sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Ahead, apart from the stairwell, stood a broad water tower, and a large antenna rose from the same foundation.'

highlights.text: Ahead in my line of sight, standing apart from the large water tower on the staircase with which it shares the foundation, stood a large antenna.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...hmmm."
comments: Unsure what attitude this is supposed to be. Doesn't sound *that* cheerful. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The subdued reaction of interest or mild admiration is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: まだ未完成のアンテナ。
adjudicated.en: A still unfinished antenna,
adjudicated.assessment: The antenna's unfinished state is preserved as a fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 足りない部品と知識。
adjudicated.en: components and knowledge both insufficient.
adjudicated.assessment: The shortages of both components and knowledge are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: それらを前向きな気持ちでもって補いながら、少しずつ形にしてきた。
adjudicated.en: Yet little by little it was taking shape, as that insufficiency was being supplemented by proactive feelings,
adjudicated.assessment: Gradually giving the project shape while compensating for the shortages with optimism is retained despite the passive, highly literal construction.

adjudicated.jp: たった一人の少女が。
adjudicated.en: those of a single solitary girl.
comments: Solitude still focus. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The delayed subject—a single girl working alone—is present, though the English attaches her grammatically to the preceding 'feelings' rather than directly to the act of construction.

adjudicated.jp: その、たった一人の少女は。
adjudicated.en: And that single solitary girl, right now,
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated focus on that one solitary girl is preserved as the subject of the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: 今、風に抱かれてアンテナと立っている。
adjudicated.en: stands with the antenna, cradled in the wind.
adjudicated.assessment: Her standing with the antenna while embraced by the wind is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 嫉妬するほどに、憧れる。
adjudicated.en: Admiration, so much it becomes jealousy.
comments: For her ability to escape. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Admiration intense enough to become jealousy is preserved in fragmentary form.

adjudicated.jp: 宮澄見里。
adjudicated.en: It's Miyasumi Misato,
adjudicated.assessment: The full name is reproduced and linked to the identification completed by the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: 見里先輩、だ。
adjudicated.en: Misato-senpai.
adjudicated.assessment: The familiar given-name-plus-senior form of identification is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「せんぱーい！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Senpaaai!"
adjudicated.assessment: The elongated call to the senior is reproduced directly.

adjudicated.jp: 呼びかけると、吹き巻く風に膜状になった黒髪が、大きくうねる。
adjudicated.en: I called out to her, and the black hair that the cradling wind had made so membranous twisted about grandiosely.
comments: See book. Otherwise: yuck. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Calling out and the black hair spreading sheet-like and undulating dramatically in the swirling wind remain recognizable. 'Cradling' reverses the force of 吹き巻く, while 'membranous' and 'twisted grandiosely' distort the visual motion.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'When I called out, her black hair, spread like a sheet by the swirling wind, billowed dramatically.'

adjudicated.jp: こっちを向く。
adjudicated.en: Turning this way,
adjudicated.assessment: Her turning toward the speaker is preserved, though the English leaves the subject implicit in a dangling participle.

adjudicated.jp: つよい風が、つやめく長髪を激流のようにする。
adjudicated.en: the strong wind made her glossy long hair as if a raging stream.
adjudicated.assessment: The strong wind turning her glossy long hair into something like a raging current is preserved despite the incomplete comparison.

adjudicated.jp: 見里先輩は苦労しつつ髪の流れを手で割って、顔をのぞかせた。
adjudicated.en: With difficulty, Misato-senpai parted the flow of her hair with a hand, so her face would peek out.
adjudicated.assessment: Her difficultly parting the flow of hair with one hand to reveal her face is conveyed accurately.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is represented directly at the resolved source occurrence.

adjudicated.jp: 早くも強みを増しつつある陽光のもと、惚けた表情が張りつく。
adjudicated.en: An expression of engrossment clings to her face, under the sunlight already growing in strength.
comments: As in, she's lost in her flight. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 惚けた表情 is a blank, dazed, or absent expression, not one of engrossment or deep absorption. The substitution changes the visible emotional state even though the strengthening sunlight and expression clinging to her face are retained.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'A dazed expression clung to her face beneath the sunlight already gathering strength.'

highlights.text: engrossment

adjudicated.jp: 夏日のうすらいとなって。
adjudicated.en: The date of Summer's lease is coming to an end,
comments: Usurai is a really pretentious way of saying "the season is ending": http://nihongohaomosiroi.seesaa.net/article/159092872.html (Japanese) so have some Shakespeare instead. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: うすらい is the poetic word for thin ice, and the next sentence explicitly continues the image by saying it will melt in an instant. The English replaces that local simile with an imported Shakespearean phrase about summer's lease and invents the season's ending.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Like thin ice on a summer day.'

highlights.text: The date of Summer's lease is coming to an end,

adjudicated.jp: だからそれは、一瞬でとけおちるのだと知っていた。
adjudicated.en: and therefore I know how that would melt off in an instant.
comments: This line just makes me laugh. I'm sort of wagering it's intentional. Of course he knows her face would melt off, she's about to 'build' her smile. Like Taichi does, according to her. If she's not projecting. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His knowing that the expression would melt away in an instant is preserved, completing the preceding image despite a tense shift.
The wordless questioning reaction is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ふっくらと色づく唇が、言葉を形作ってほころびる。
adjudicated.en: Her plump reddening lips begin to part as words begin to be formed.
adjudicated.assessment: Her full, colored lips parting as they form words are conveyed directly.

adjudicated.jp: びょう、と耳元に怒鳴りつける突風が、しかし呟きをかき消した。
adjudicated.en: A gust of wind near my ears drowned out what was but a murmur with its roar.
adjudicated.assessment: The roaring gust at his ears drowning out the murmur is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 唇の動きで、なにを言っているのかはわかる。
adjudicated.en: By the movement of her lips I knew what she had said.
comments: He can't read lips. He's just hallucinating the words, see CCB0005. Notice how we don't actually hear them. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Understanding what she said from the movement of her lips is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: にっこり笑って、応じた。
adjudicated.en: Grinning broadly, I replied,
adjudicated.assessment: Smiling and replying are preserved; 'grinning broadly' is slightly brasher than にっこり but remains functional.

adjudicated.jp: 「来ちゃいましたー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I have cooome!"
adjudicated.assessment: The playful elongated announcement that he has come is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぺけくん……」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Peke-kun..."
comments: 'distant voice'. But such directions don't seem followed? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The nickname and familiar suffix are reproduced directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「どーもー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Hellooo!"
adjudicated.assessment: The elongated casual greeting is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 両手を突き上げて叫ぶ。
adjudicated.en: I thrust both hands to the sky and shout.
comments: See CCA0010, supposing "I surrender". Also means "to pressure one's superiors", interestingly enough. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Thrusting both hands upward and shouting are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: と、先輩の目尻が下がる。
adjudicated.en: And, the corners of Senpai's eyes fell.
adjudicated.assessment: The corners of her eyes lowering as her expression softens is preserved literally and completed by the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: コマ落としのフィルムを見るように、柔和な面持ちに移ろっていく。
adjudicated.en: As if watching a time-lapse film, a look of gentleness fades in.
comments: Obvious artefaction. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her expression transitioning frame by frame into gentleness is conveyed; 'time-lapse' is not exact for dropped-frame film but preserves the visible stepwise change.

adjudicated.jp: 「どーもー！」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Heeellooo!"
adjudicated.assessment: The echoed elongated greeting is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 応じてきた。
adjudicated.en: So came the answer.
adjudicated.assessment: That she answers him is preserved despite the inverted, stilted English.

adjudicated.jp: いつもの彼女。
adjudicated.en: The girl that she is always.
comments: Somewhat recurring. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The observation that she is back to her usual self is recoverable from the literal fragment.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうしましたかー、ぺけくーん？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "What can I help you wiiith, Peke-kuuun?"
comments: The shouts are 99% in the text, sorry. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The elongated question asking what he needs and the nickname are both preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「パンツ見えてますよー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I can see your pantieees!"
comments: Although pretentiousness makes me laugh on its own, the entirety of it was just as setup for this punchline. Besides requiring understanding what the hell he's talking about, the reason this thing is so damn hard to translate is because of the absolute tonal precision some parts demand, like this. Although pretentiousness for the sake of laughter seems to be in Tanaka's style, and it further continues the undercurrent of criticism towards this kind of writing when used for its own sake, it's worked in the plot: this is Taichi not taking this seriously in the slightest and refusing to let heavy moods settle in. Later on, this will become uneasy and outright cringe-worthy. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The shouted warning or tease that her underwear is visible is conveyed directly.

adjudicated.jp: なんてことを言ってみたり。
adjudicated.en: Why do I keep saying this stuff...
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a light narrative aside equivalent to 'or so I tried saying' after the preceding line. The English turns it into a self-directed question and invents repeated habitual behavior with 'keep,' changing both function and tone.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Or so I tried saying.'

highlights.text: Why do I keep saying this stuff...

adjudicated.jp: どうせまともに聞こえまい。
adjudicated.en: Whatever, she probably won't hear that right.
comments: "she probably hasn't heard it at all" + "she would dishonestly act as if she hasn't heard it". Bluff. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The assumption that she probably cannot hear it properly anyway is preserved in colloquial but awkward English.

adjudicated.jp: パンツは実際に見えていて、もっと近かったら理性がやばい。
adjudicated.en: I can really see her panties, and if I'd been any closer my rationality'd be in trouble.
comments: Vs. what he did with Touko just before. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The fact that the underwear is visible and that greater proximity would endanger his self-control are both preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 強風からパンチラの可能性を充分考慮しており、前もって心構えをしていたため、
adjudicated.en: Having given plenty of prior consideration to the possibility of the strong wind giving me a show of panties, and therefore steeled myself for that beforehand,
adjudicated.assessment: His anticipating the possibility of a wind-caused glimpse and mentally preparing himself in advance are preserved in an unwieldy continuing clause.

adjudicated.jp: そのすらりとしていてなお肉感的な三年生女子の罪深い太股と、股間部を包む男心を鷲掴む抗えない逆三角の情熱を目撃してしまっても、どうにか平静でいられた。
adjudicated.en: I was therefore still somewhat calm despite ending up witness of the well-proportioned and furthermore sensual sinful thighs of this third year girl, as well as bearing the brunt of the passion of the reverse triangle that like an eagle unopposably ensnares the male heart.
comments: This line was split, but the whole description's been moved to NVL. Sinful, of course, meant literally. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately excessive description of the older student's slender yet sensual thighs, the inverted triangle covering her crotch, and his managing to remain calm survives despite highly unidiomatic syntax and an over-literal rendering of 鷲掴む.

adjudicated.jp: ※男心を鷲掴む抗えない逆三角の情熱……太一語。女性用下着（ショーツ）の意。
adjudicated.en:
* "Passion of the reverse triangle that like
an eagle unopposably ensnares the male heart"
comments: See CCZAS. We're in a Post-Babel world too, it seems, that humans have their own languages. Eagles because Tolkien (actually Bible, but let's not go into the advanced stuff). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source is an explanatory note: it identifies the extravagant phrase as the narrator's coinage and states that it means women's underwear. The English repeats only a strained rendering of the coined phrase and omits both pieces of explanation, so the note no longer performs its defining function.
adjudicated.remedy: Retain the coined phrase, then state that it is the narrator's term for women's underwear or panties.

highlights.text:
* "Passion of the reverse triangle that like
an eagle unopposably ensnares the male heart"

adjudicated.jp: そうでなければ、あの肉欲の罪過を誘引せしめる三年生女子の臀部に、俺ごときのゴザ虫が欲情を抑えられるはずもなく。
adjudicated.en: Without doing that, there would be no way for stinkbugs like I to ever restrain their sexual appetites when confronted with the offenseful carnal desires induced by this third year girl's loins.
comments: All the insect stuff means him being a stinkbug is also meant literally. Notice that this is meant in reaction to his steeling himself, not the standards changing. ...though I suspect ambiguity as both work, really. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that otherwise a lowly bedbug like the narrator could not restrain his arousal before the older student's buttocks, which invite the sin of lust. The English changes the self-deprecating insect, turns singular self-reference into plural stinkbugs, replaces buttocks with loins, and makes the girl's body appear to possess or induce carnal desires rather than provoke his.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep the narrator as the single desiring subject and preserve the comic self-abasement, the buttocks, and the conditional relation.

highlights.text: Without doing that, there would be no way for stinkbugs like I to ever restrain their sexual appetites when confronted with the offenseful carnal desires induced by this third year girl's loins.

adjudicated.jp: 「なーにー？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "What is iiit?"
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out casual question is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「パンツ売ってくださーい！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Please sell me what you wear!!!"
comments: Please sell me what you wear! -> please bake me some bread? -> Please buy what I wear (see CCA0013) Original pun is: pantsu utte kudasai (please sell me your panties) -> pan tsukutte kudasai (please bake me some bread) -> [ore no] pantsu katte kunnai (please buy my panties). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The request explicitly asks her to sell him her panties. Replacing パンツ with the generic 'what you wear' removes the underwear request and destroys the audible パンツ売って／パン作って misunderstanding that produces the next reply.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an explicit underwear request and rebuild the adjacent English exchange so the mistaken bread request remains audibly motivated.

highlights.text: Please sell me what you wear!!!

adjudicated.jp: 「パン作ってください？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Please bake me some bread?"
adjudicated.assessment: The mistaken request to make bread is translated literally. Its functional connection to the preceding line fails there, not in this reply itself.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "!!!???"
adjudicated.assessment: The punctuation-only shock and confusion are reproduced directly.

adjudicated.jp: 八割方聞こえテールッ！（メキシカン調）
adjudicated.en: Seh can uhnderstand meeh at eh nearly 80% rahteh! (Mexican accent)
comments: Randomly foreign. I suppose American would be too obvious. I just fed the translation through this http://www.oddcast.com/home/demos/tts/tts_example.php?sitepal (Spanish language/Javier's voice) and transcribed. More importantly: this is an eight (80% is written hachi-wari), and she's sort of misunderstanding him. It's a very very early reading key: Eight Means Wrong. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source exclaims that she can hear about eighty percent of what he says, delivered in a Mexican-style voice. The English instead says that an unspecified 'she' can understand the speaker and supplies an invented phonetic caricature, changing person, action, and delivery.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep first-person perception and the approximate eighty-percent figure, with a restrained stage direction for the stylized accent.

highlights.text: Seh can uhnderstand meeh at eh nearly 80% rahteh! (Mexican accent)

adjudicated.jp: 「ひひひひひ昼ご飯、一緒に食べましょうよー！！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Lu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lunch, let us go eat it togetheeer!!!"
comments: This should be like 8:30, time screw or not, so it's just a really panicky response. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The panicked stammer and invitation to eat lunch together are both retained, though the English stammer and phrasing are awkward.

adjudicated.jp: 「おー、いーですよー！」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Ohhh, that is fiiine!"
adjudicated.assessment: The cheerful elongated acceptance is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ぐるぐる拳を振り上げる先輩。
adjudicated.en: Senpai spins round and round the fist she raised upwards.
comments: For some reason ぐるぐる拳 comes up as Hokuto no Ken's seminal Atatata thousand-punch. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The senior's circular fist motion and raised arm are both recoverable, although the English word order makes the movement unnecessarily difficult to picture.

adjudicated.jp: 「でもパンなんて焼けないですよー、わたしー」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But I cannot bake bread, I cannot!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her drawn-out protest that she cannot bake bread is preserved, with repetition used to approximate the trailing self-reference.

adjudicated.jp: 「そ、そりゃあ残念！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Th-, that is too bad!"
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered declaration of disappointment is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「ごめんねー！」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Sorryyy!"
adjudicated.assessment: The friendly elongated apology is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: なんとか誤魔化した。
adjudicated.en: Deceived somehow.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator's somehow managing to bluff or gloss over the situation remains recoverable, although the subjectless English fragment is unnatural.

adjudicated.jp: やばかった……。
adjudicated.en: That was close...
adjudicated.assessment: The brief retrospective relief that the situation was dangerous or close is naturally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 俺のダーティーな部分は先輩には秘密なのだ。
adjudicated.en: I keep my Dirty side secret from Senpai.
comments: English. He's so gone. And she totally heard him, too. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His determination to keep his dirty side secret from the senior is preserved. The capitalized loanword is eccentric but mirrors the source's conspicuous katakana expression.

adjudicated.jp: この人に軽蔑されるのは、ちょっとばかりつらい。
adjudicated.en: Being despised by this one person would be just a little tiny bit heart-breaking.
comments: See CCA0016, where he'll ask her if she despises him for doing what should technically have nothing to do with this dirty side of his. Or does it? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The prospect of being despised by this person hurting him is retained, but 'heart-breaking' gives the modest ちょっとばかりつらい a more dramatic emotional commitment than the source states.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a restrained phrase such as 'would hurt a little.'

adjudicated.jp: 一人だった俺を……放送部に誘ってくれた人だから。
adjudicated.en: Because when I was alone... it was she who invited me to the Broadcast Club.
adjudicated.assessment: The causal explanation that she invited him into the club when he was alone is preserved fully.

adjudicated.jp: 「それが用事だったのですかー？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Is that what you were here fooor?"
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out question asking whether that was his business is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「ついでに部活に来ましたー！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "While I was at it I also came here for cluuub!"
adjudicated.assessment: His elongated claim that he also came for club activities while he was at it is preserved, despite clumsy English ordering.

adjudicated.jp: 「つ、ついで？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "W-, while you were...?"
adjudicated.assessment: Her startled repetition of 'while you were at it' is recognizable, though the English trails off instead of repeating the key expression cleanly.

adjudicated.jp: 顔がひきつる。
adjudicated.en: Her face twitched.
comments: Intended to be read that she's angered at her casual dismissal of club on first pass; she's actually annoyed that he came to club at all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The facial twitch or stiffening is conveyed directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「言葉のアヤ子さんです」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Something I got from Didnotmentat Literallia-san!"
comments: Kotoba no Ayako-san, just a widespread pun, doesn't seem to have a specific origin. Since it's an anthropomorphism, of which there are a fair few (may or may not include Youko), now she's a Family Circus running gag. See CCD1001 for Tomoki using this normally. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source turns 言葉の綾, 'a figure of speech,' into the woman's name Ayako as a comic excuse. The invented name does not make 'figure of speech' or 'I did not mean it literally' intelligible in English, so the line's immediate repair function and its name pun are both lost.
adjudicated.remedy: Build an English feminine-name pun whose surrounding wording clearly means that 'while I was at it' was only a figure of speech.

highlights.text: Didnotmentat Literallia-san!

adjudicated.jp: 「はぁ……ちょっとお待ちくださーい」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Sigh... please be patient some mooore!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her sigh and request that he wait a little are preserved; 'be patient some more' shifts the wording but retains the practical request.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい、お待たせです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Yes, here I am now."
adjudicated.assessment: お待たせです conventionally acknowledges that the other person has been kept waiting: 'thanks for waiting' or 'sorry to keep you waiting.' The English instead announces the speaker's arrival and omits that acknowledgment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'There—thanks for waiting' or an equivalent acknowledgment.

highlights.text: Misato: "Yes, here I am now."

adjudicated.jp: 両手を前で重ねて、にっこりと微笑む。
adjudicated.en: She smiles brightly, her hands overlapped in front of her.
adjudicated.assessment: Her overlapping both hands in front of herself and smiling brightly are accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 脳内フォトシ○ップが立ち上がる。
adjudicated.en: Launching intracranial Photosh*p (pirated copy).
comments: HACK that addition is from the 360 version. Nice censorship, by the way. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source jokes that the narrator's mental Photo○shop launches. The parenthetical claim that the copy is pirated is newly invented and changes the joke without textual support.
adjudicated.remedy: Remove the piracy parenthesis and retain only the censored mental image-editing software gag.

highlights.text: (pirated copy)

adjudicated.jp: ０．１秒で起動だ。脳内だから。
adjudicated.en: Startup completes in 0.1 seconds. That's why it's intracranial.
comments: That would still make it about 1 second. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source gives the mental location as the reason for the 0.1-second startup. 'That's why it's intracranial' reverses the causal direction, making the startup speed explain why the process is in his head.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that it starts in 0.1 seconds because it is running in his head.

highlights.text: Startup completes in 0.1 seconds. That's why it's intracranial.

adjudicated.jp: まずパスで先輩の顔部分を背景から切り抜く。
adjudicated.en: First pass: extract Senpai's face from background.
adjudicated.assessment: The first editing pass, cutting the senior's face out from its background, is preserved accurately.

adjudicated.jp: アイドルグラビアから、似たような格好をしているヌード写真を探す。
adjudicated.en: Searching for a nude picture of a gravure idol in a similar position.
comments: The implication is that he knows them all by memory, i.e. supermemory. But perfect callback, considering. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Searching gravure material for a nude photograph in a similar pose is retained, though the English is an isolated participial fragment.

adjudicated.jp: まさにその格好をしている一枚があった。
adjudicated.en: Of course there is one picture of exactly that pose.
adjudicated.assessment: Finding one image in precisely that pose is preserved. 'Of course' and the present tense add tone but do not materially change the discovery.

adjudicated.jp: だいぶ古いが、相撲取りとつきあったり激痩せしたりママが出張ったりして有名になったらしいアイドルのヌード写真集だ。南無。
adjudicated.en: It's quite old, but it's from a nude photo-book of an Idol who got sort of famous for having dated a sumo wrestler, extreme weight loss, and some standout issues with her mom. Amen!
comments: Credit to here: http://www6.ocn.ne.jp/~rejina/cc/motoneta.html here she is: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rie_Miyazawa See book on this. Notice the amen. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The old nude photobook and the three tabloid-like reasons for the idol's fame are retained. The mother's conspicuous involvement becomes vaguely described as 'issues,' but the list and closing mock prayer survive.

adjudicated.jp: ともかく、先輩の顔レイヤーとその写真を合成する。
adjudicated.en: Anyway, composing the layer with Senpai's face into said photo.
adjudicated.assessment: Compositing the senior's face layer into the photograph is conveyed accurately despite fragmentary English.

adjudicated.jp: いろいろといじりながら、接合部の余分な部分をぼかしながら消していく。
adjudicated.en: While fiddling all sorts, erase while smoothening the excess parts in the areas that connect the two.
adjudicated.assessment: Fiddling with the image while blurring away excess material at the joins is fully recoverable, although the repeated English participles are clumsy.

adjudicated.jp: 胸の部分が実際とは違うと思われるので、もっとふくよかな美乳を探して合成する。
adjudicated.en: The chest part appears in truth wrong, therefore compositing with plumper and beautiful breasts.
comments: Indeed Rie is faaar less plump than Misato. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The judgment that the chest differs from reality and the search for fuller, attractive breasts to composite are retained, despite malformed syntax.

adjudicated.jp: ついでに生肌が露出している腕と脚の部分も、先輩のものを使う。
adjudicated.en: While I'm at it, I use Senpai's tone from the exposed skin on the arms and legs.
comments: No way that "while I'm at it" is coincidental. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that for the exposed arms and legs he also uses the senior's own body parts. The English instead says he samples her skin tone, changing a component replacement into color matching.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he uses the senior's own exposed arms and legs as well.

highlights.text: tone from the exposed skin

adjudicated.jp: 全体を見ながら、光加減を調整したり影を描き加えたりする。
adjudicated.en: With an eye on the whole composition, regulate the excesses and defects of light, and draw shadows.
adjudicated.assessment: Reviewing the whole composition, adjusting the light, and drawing in shadows are all present. 'Excesses and defects' is unnecessary interpretation but does not alter the procedure materially.

adjudicated.jp: 肌の色の差は、薄い黄色の新規レイヤーを重ね、描画モードをソフトラインにすることで統一した。
adjudicated.en: As for the difference in skin color, add a pale yellow into a new layer, and consolidate using Soft Line Blending Mode.
comments: That's the correct translation according to the Adobe help pages, except it should be soft LINE blending mode (ソフトライト not ソフトライン). There's no Soft Line mode documented, so either it's a typo that went unfixed as far as the 360 edition, or Taichi's talking out of his ass. Which seems likely regardless. Does he even know how to use Photoshop...? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source names the image editor's Soft Light blending mode. 'Soft Line' is not that mode and gives an incorrect technical instruction, even though the new pale-yellow layer and the goal of unifying skin color are retained.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Soft Light blending mode.'

highlights.text: Soft Line Blending Mode

adjudicated.jp: 背景がないのは寂しいので、先輩のレイヤーの下に厳かな聖堂画像を張った。
adjudicated.en: Because without scenery it looks sort of lonely, I pasted the image of an austere church nave in the layer below Senpai's.
comments: Original BG was a wall. That's an explicit reference to a Christian Church, by the way. So, on this little irrelevant aside, besides having an external real-life person provide multiple overlaps with this character, showing Taichi can have perfect recall at times, seeing him composite a sexual situation from nothing in what takes a few seconds for him, but is a long time for the outside, there are two religious references, one that in practice can go both ways (the amen), one that can't be but Christian (this). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The lonely lack of a background, the solemn church interior, and placement beneath the senior's layer are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 完璧だ。
adjudicated.en: Perfect.
adjudicated.assessment: The terse declaration of perfection is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 十年使えるエロコラ、ここに爆誕。
adjudicated.en: A sexy 'shopped image that will last decades has here its explosive birth.
comments: I can't find that word used seriously outside of the Pokemon 2000 movie, so I got the word from the Wikipedia literal translation of the title. Will recur. No, seriously, it will. Although ten isn't as recurring as 7 or 8, ten years is cross-years. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 十年 is specifically ten years. 'Decades' changes that comic quantitative boast to an indefinite period of twenty years or more, while the source's explosive-birth register is otherwise retained.
adjudicated.remedy: Call it an erotic composite good for ten years.

highlights.text: will last decades

adjudicated.jp: すぐさま俺はそれを脳内ＨＤＤの『数学課題』フォルダ内にある『Ｓ級』フォルダに保存した。
adjudicated.en: I promptly saved it in my intracranial hard drive, inside the folder "Level S" under the folder "Math Homework".
comments: That's ridiculous! You need at least THREE subfolders for this! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The prompt save to the S-rank folder inside the mental hard drive's Math Homework folder is preserved precisely.

adjudicated.jp: Ｓ→Ａ→Ｂ→Ｃ→Ｄと区分けされている。
adjudicated.en: The levels are ordered: S→A→B→C→D.
comments: This is important mainly in how Yutaka shares this, and may have been the one to teach him for that matter, but it's still interesting in how he makes stuff up in his mind about the people while simultaneously losing all contact with the world, and being caught by surprise, see in a moment. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The S-through-D classification order is reproduced directly.

adjudicated.jp: Ｓが最強。Ｄが最低。
adjudicated.en: S is the strongest, D is the weakest.
comments: Redundant... or is it? "Saitei" is typical Tsunderese for "disgusting". It may be that Ds are where he keeps his really nasty stuff. Sorta-literal, see CCA0007. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The highest and lowest ranks are identified correctly; 'strongest' and 'weakest' preserve the comic ranking language adequately.

adjudicated.jp: 現実のパソコンでもそう区分けされている。
adjudicated.en: My real PC is also organized that way.
comments: Wondering if Youko's is, but more importantly, given his emphasis on Wacchi, wondering if his real PC is also full of photoshopped porn images of his friends. That'd be quite creepy, but not unexpected. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The same classification existing on his physical computer is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: そして俺の遺言状の文面には、まず最初にこう書かれている。
adjudicated.en: Thus, the very first thing that's written at the beginning of my last will and testament goes,
comments: So he HAS a will. Was it even executed? Inquiring minds want to know! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The setup that the first line of his will reads as follows is retained, although the English ends in a loose comma.

adjudicated.jp: 『何も考えずにＨＤＤを捨ててください（閲覧・形見分け絶対禁止、したら全霊力をかけて呪う）』
adjudicated.en: 'Please dispose of my hard disk drive without even a single thought (inspection or utilization as memento mori are strictly forbidden, violators shall be cursed to the full extent of the powers of my soul.)'
comments: Ironically, if he's not dead, at the end he'd be a ghost of sorts... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: 形見分け is the distribution of a deceased person's belongings as keepsakes. 'Utilization as memento mori' instead suggests using the drive as a reminder of mortality and loses the prohibition on dividing it among survivors.
adjudicated.remedy: Forbid both inspection and distribution as a keepsake, followed by the threatened curse.

highlights.text: utilization as memento mori

adjudicated.jp: 数学課題フォルダだけは、決して人に見られてはいけない。
adjudicated.en: In no way can anyone be allowed to look in my Math Homework folder,
adjudicated.assessment: The absolute need to prevent anyone from seeing the Math Homework folder is preserved, with the sentence intentionally continuing into the next unit.

adjudicated.jp: なぜなら数学課題フォルダこそまさに、俺の野生衝動そのものだから。
adjudicated.en: the reason being that said math homework folder is my wildest impulse incarnate.
comments: His wildest impulse contains PORN. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The folder as the embodiment of his wild impulse is retained, but 'wildest' invents a superlative absent from 野生衝動 and intensifies the ranking claim.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'my wild impulse incarnate' without the superlative.

adjudicated.jp: そう。
adjudicated.en: Yes.
adjudicated.assessment: The brief emphatic transition is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 数学課題フォルダは禁断にして秘められた聖域～ＳＡＮＣＴＵＡＲＹ～。
adjudicated.en:
My math homework folder I know as,
The Forbidden Secreted Holy Ground
～SANCTUARY～
comments: Should sound like a bad nukige title now. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The folder as a forbidden, secret sanctuary and the conspicuous English label are all retained, though the sentence is syntactically strained.

adjudicated.jp: 「数学課題フォルダがどうかしましたか？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "What has happened to your maths homework folder?"
adjudicated.assessment: The question asking whether something is wrong with the Math Homework folder is preserved. The regional spelling does not affect source accuracy.

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "KHH!!!???"
comments: Let's go with snakelike. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The punctuation expresses a choked, shocked reaction, so a brief nonlexical sound is defensible, but the specific 'KHH' vocalization is supplied by the translator rather than stated.
adjudicated.remedy: Use punctuation or a minimally committed choked sound.

adjudicated.jp: 無意識に喋っテータッ！！（メキ略）
adjudicated.en: Ieh spokeh unconziouhslyyy!!! (Mexy (abbr.))
comments: Would've worked better if the term'd been longer... I guess the joke's that... well, they can't all be winners (coughs suspiciously). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The exclamation that he spoke unconsciously and the abbreviated return of the stylized Mexican delivery are retained. The phonetic English is ungainly but keeps the explicit performance cue.

adjudicated.jp: 「レディ、わたくしめになにか手伝えることはありませんか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Lady, is there then nothing with which your worthless servant could perhaps assist You with?"
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-deferential address and offer by her worthless servant to help are both preserved, albeit in overcomplicated English.

adjudicated.jp: 恭しく指を取る。
adjudicated.en: I take her forefingers with extreme deference.
adjudicated.assessment: Reverently taking her finger or fingers is preserved; specifying forefingers is narrower than 指 but remains compatible with the gesture. The binding uses the registered normalized source match.

adjudicated.jp: 先輩は平然としている。
adjudicated.en: Senpai remains calm.
comments: No rejection to physical contact. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The senior remaining perfectly composed is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「でも、もう学校の時間ですよ？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But... it is about time for school, right?"
comments: She's escaping reality; unless he is. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The reminder that it is already time for school is preserved naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 小首をかしげる仕草が犯罪的だ。
adjudicated.en: That act of slightly tilting her neck is criminal.
adjudicated.assessment: The small head tilt being criminally charming is retained, although 'tilting her neck' names the movement less idiomatically.

adjudicated.jp: 「学校など」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "School and all that, right!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source is a lofty dismissive fragment, roughly 'School, of all things...' or 'As for school...' The English adds a tag-like 'right!' and turns the unfinished dismissal into an oddly affirmative sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Keep a clipped, dismissive fragment such as 'School? Bah.' or 'School, of all things...'

adjudicated.jp: おおげさに首を振って、笑い捨てる。
adjudicated.en: I shake my head with exaggeration and smile at that idea.
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated head shake is preserved, but 笑い捨てる is a dismissive or scornful laugh, not merely smiling at an idea. The stronger performative rejection is weakened.
adjudicated.remedy: Have him shake his head theatrically and laugh the idea off.

adjudicated.jp: 「今あなたを手伝うこと以外、どのような優先すべきことがありましょうや」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "What priority exists outside of helping you now?"
comments: Back to formal. He's trying to work himself back in her graces, not necessarily because classes don't exist anymore. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-grand question that nothing could take priority over helping her now is preserved, though the English is compressed.

adjudicated.jp: 戸惑う先輩も素敵だ。
adjudicated.en: Senpai is wonderful when bewildered, as well.
adjudicated.assessment: His appreciation of the senior even when bewildered is retained exactly.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぜひ子孫繁栄のお手伝いも小生めに一任してはいただけまいか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Shall you not entrust this most lowest servant with assisting you even in regards to the certainty of the perpetuation of your descendance?"
comments: 120 characters to ask "can I fuck you?" Also see CCA0003 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The hyper-formal request to entrust the humble speaker with helping propagate her descendants is preserved, including its deliberately excessive register.

adjudicated.jp: 「えっ？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Eh?"
adjudicated.assessment: The brief surprised response is reproduced directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「あわわ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "AhWahWah!"
comments: Girly speech is hardest, unfortunately, it just doesn't exist in English. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The flustered nonlexical reaction is represented functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 慌てて口を押さえる。
adjudicated.en: I restrain my mouth in a frenzy.
adjudicated.assessment: The source describes hurriedly covering his mouth with a hand. 'Restraining' the mouth neither specifies covering it nor clearly describes a physical gesture, and 'in a frenzy' overstates the simple hurried reaction.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he hurriedly clapped a hand over his mouth.

highlights.text: I restrain my mouth in a frenzy.

adjudicated.jp: 思ったことが口から漏れる癖、なんとかせんとなあ。
adjudicated.en: I reeeally gotta do something about this bad habit of passing thoughts through the mouth.
comments: Can't source this dialect-sounding expression. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His need to do something about the habit of letting thoughts slip from his mouth is fully recoverable, despite the mechanical phrasing.

adjudicated.jp: 「アンテナ、だいぶ形になりましたね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "The antenna seems to have mostly taken shape, has it."
adjudicated.assessment: The observation that the antenna has largely taken shape is preserved, with only an awkward tag ending.

adjudicated.jp: 「うん。頑張りました」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Yes, I gave it my all!"
comments: No problem changing topic. She knows he's... like this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her confirmation that she worked hard is preserved naturally.

adjudicated.jp: 「もう完成ですか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Is it complete already?"
adjudicated.assessment: The question asking whether it is already complete is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 「……まだ全然なんですよ、これが」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "...not at all yet, it is not."
adjudicated.assessment: Her admission that it is nowhere near finished is retained, although the English repeats the negative awkwardly.

adjudicated.jp: 業者が組み立ててくれるはずだったアンテナ。
adjudicated.en: The antenna should have been assembled by the contractors,
adjudicated.assessment: The antenna having been supposed to be assembled by contractors is preserved as the opening of the continuing sentence.

adjudicated.jp: 搬入だけされて、うち捨てられた。
adjudicated.en: but it was just brought in and then abandoned.
comments: Yutaka incident -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Its being delivered and then abandoned is retained accurately, completing the preceding clause.

adjudicated.jp: 「専門家じゃありませんし、だましだまし組み立ててます」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "I am not a specialist, but by hook or by crook I am putting it together."
comments: Lit. 'every trick in the book'. "Following the book closely" would fit Misato's apparent personality better, but since this is a finery that reveals the truth - the term literally reads "deceiving deceiving" - this is closest. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her lack of specialist expertise and incremental improvisation while assembling it are retained. 'By hook or by crook' is broader but preserves making do.

adjudicated.jp: 「本体はいいとしても、配線や調整は手つかずですし」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "The frame may be fine, but I have not laid hand on the wiring or the tuning."
adjudicated.assessment: The main body being one matter while wiring and adjustment remain untouched is preserved, despite stiff collocation.

adjudicated.jp: 「あらら」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Oh my my."
comments: More girly-ish. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mild dismayed reaction is reproduced functionally.

adjudicated.jp: 残念ながら、俺にもそういう知識はない。
adjudicated.en: Sad as it may be, I'm no expert on those things either.
comments: Notice the complete lack of even the idea of calling Youko in. Who is. Maybe. If she exists. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His regrettable lack of that kind of knowledge is preserved. 'No expert' is slightly weaker than having no such knowledge but does not reverse the practical conclusion.

adjudicated.jp: 「……手伝えること、なさそうですね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...seems unlikely that I could help you, then."
adjudicated.assessment: His conclusion that there appears to be nothing he can help with is preserved, though the English construction is formal.

adjudicated.jp: 「お気持ちだけで」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "I appreciate the thought."
adjudicated.assessment: The polite acknowledgment that the thought alone is enough is naturally localized.

adjudicated.jp: ちらと見やった先輩の手が、傷だらけだった。
adjudicated.en: I chanced to look closely at Senpai's hands, and they were covered with scratches.
comments: This is what she uses in replacement of the wrist slashing. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: ちらと見やる is to cast a quick glance. 'Chanced to look closely' changes an intentional brief glance into an accidental close inspection, altering both attention and duration.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he glanced over and saw that the senior's hands were covered in cuts or scratches.

highlights.text: chanced to look closely

adjudicated.jp: あー。
adjudicated.en: Ahhh,
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out realizing reaction is preserved as the start of a continuing thought.

adjudicated.jp: 苦労しちゃってまあ。
adjudicated.en: she's having a really hard time then...
adjudicated.assessment: His sympathetic recognition that she has been struggling is preserved, if conversationally awkward.

adjudicated.jp: モニターひとつ持ち上げられない細腕なのに。
adjudicated.en: When her slender arms could never lift up but one of those transceivers.
comments: Although 'monitor' is technically the correct word, it makes it sound like she's carrying computer monitors around, which have very little to do with an antenna that has no video feeds whatsoever and very little apparent need for any. Someone should probably tell the guy who draws BGs before he fills the Club Room with actual--- whoops. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says her slender arms cannot lift even a single monitor. 'Could never lift up but one' conventionally means she could lift only one, reversing the scalar negative, and 'transceiver' replaces the monitor without support.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that her slender arms cannot even lift a single monitor.

highlights.text: When her slender arms could never lift up but one of those transceivers.

adjudicated.jp: 「あの、先輩」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Uhm, Senpai."
adjudicated.assessment: The hesitant address to the senior is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Yes?"
adjudicated.assessment: The polite questioning reply is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「どうして一人でやろうとするんです？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Why are you trying to this all alone?"
adjudicated.assessment: The question asking why she is trying to do it alone is fully recoverable despite the missing English verb.

adjudicated.jp: 「みんなだっているのに。召集かけたらいいじゃないですか」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Because everybody is here. Should you not just call us to assembly?"
adjudicated.assessment: The point that everyone else is present and could simply be summoned is preserved, though 'call us to assembly' is overly formal.

adjudicated.en: Misato: "...hmmm."
adjudicated.assessment: The hesitant hum is preserved directly.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたし、部長だったりしますし」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Well, I am the President after all."
adjudicated.assessment: Her understated reminder that she is the club president is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぶっちょがやらねば誰もついてこないでしょう？」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "'Cause if the Prez don't do it, nobody'll come along, is that not it?"
comments: Sorta lapsing into accent. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The playful pronunciation of president and her claim that no one will follow unless the leader acts are preserved, despite rough tag-question grammar.

adjudicated.jp: 「いや、今でも誰もついてきてないデス……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well, right now no one is coming along, are they..."
comments: That katakana 'desu'... smells like he's saying "following you to their death". -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His dry observation that nobody is following her even now is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「ぺけくんがやってきてくれました」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "But you did come here, Peke-kun."
adjudicated.assessment: Her warm answer that he came is preserved with the nickname.

adjudicated.jp: うわ、殺し文句。
adjudicated.en: Waah, killer words.
comments: Random usages of the kanji for 'kill' will return. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His reaction to the irresistible or devastating line is recoverable from the literal 'killer words,' though the English idiom is unnatural.

adjudicated.jp: 「それに自分がやりたいというのもありますし」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "Plus there is also how I just want to do this myself."
adjudicated.assessment: Her added reason that she personally wants to do it is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしは好きなことやってるだけです」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "This is just me doing something that I like."
adjudicated.assessment: Her statement that she is simply doing what she likes is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「皆とおんなじに」
adjudicated.en: Misato: "It is the same for everybody."
adjudicated.assessment: The comparison that she is doing so just like everyone else is preserved, although the English states the equivalence more generally.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Everybody... but they are not doing anything they like doing, you know?"

adjudicated.jp: 「そうですか？」

adjudicated.jp: なんとなく。
adjudicated.en: For some reason or another.
adjudicated.assessment: Here なんとなく qualifies his belief as vague intuition: 'somehow' or 'just a feeling.' 'For some reason or another' instead suggests an unknown external cause and weakens the self-aware uncertainty.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Just a feeling' or 'Somehow.'

adjudicated.jp: 「実感わいてないだけじゃないですかね、きっと」

adjudicated.assessment: 実感がわく concerns gaining a felt sense of reality or having something sink in. The English invents suppressed 'true feelings' that are not coming out publicly, changing internal apprehension into emotional disclosure.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that the situation simply has not felt real to them yet.

highlights.text: Taichi: "It is just that their true feelings are sort of not coming out in the open, definitely."

The English invents a pig, changes the sentence into an inability to apply mascara, and provides no intelligible sound bridge to the ensuing maracas gag.

adjudicated.en: What she's thinking I don't know.

adjudicated.jp: この人は、そうたやすく本心を見せたりはしない。
adjudicated.en: This person here does not want to show her true feelings all that easily.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she does not readily reveal her true feelings; the rendering adds an explicit desire not to reveal them.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe her habitual reluctance or reserve without adding a stated intention.

adjudicated.jp: だからこそ、さっきの唖然とした顔は貴重なのであり。
adjudicated.en: That is exactly why the face of mute displeasure she made earlier is so precious.
adjudicated.assessment: The adjective describes a stunned or dumbfounded expression, not mute displeasure; the emotional content is changed.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the earlier face as stunned or dumbfounded.

adjudicated.jp: 柔和な顔は仮面でしかないんだと、俺はわかってしまうのだ。
adjudicated.en: Her gentle face is nothing but a mask, this I completely understand.
adjudicated.assessment: The underlying realization is retained, but the comma splice and fronted demonstrative produce unidiomatic English.
adjudicated.remedy: Integrate the realization as a normal subordinate clause.
